description: Compute the n-th root of any number — square root, cube root and beyond — with exact handling of negative inputs for odd roots.

faqs.a: The n-th root of x is the number r with r^n = x. For example, the cube root of 27 is 3 because 3^3 = 27.

faqs.q: Can I take an even root of a negative number?
faqs.a: Not in the real numbers — no real number squared gives a negative. The tool will tell you this and only offer complex results as a note. Odd roots of negatives are fine (e.g. ∛(−8) = −2).
The calculator raises the result back to the n-th power and shows it next to your original x, so you can confirm r^n ≈ x.

howto: Enter n, the root degree (2 for square root, 3 for cube root, …).
Read the n-th root instantly with a raise-back verification.
Note that even roots of negative numbers have no real result.
title: Nth Root Calculator
